subject: Proposed POC evaluation plan + success criteria (next steps)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 08 Apr 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed POC evaluation plan + success criteria (next steps)

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap from our side and a concrete proposal for the 4-week POC so we can align on success criteria, timelines, and owners. I attached a one-page playbook and an evaluation metrics sheet for the team to fill in.

What we heard on the call (prioritized):
- Goal: Validate Redwood Inference for semantic search and clinical note summarization in a production-like environment.
- Key constraints: PHI-safe transfer (we discussed VPC/private deployment option), average query length ~120 tokens, peak concurrency ~60 req/s.

Proposed POC scope (4 weeks):
1) Week 0 (prep, 3 days): access, test dataset handoff, infra checklist completed by Acme ops + Redwood SE.
2) Week 1 (ingest & baseline): run baseline against existing service, collect quality/latency metrics.
3) Week 2 (tuning & quantization): deploy recommended quantization profile, enable prefix caching, observe performance & cost.
4) Weeks 3–4 (stress & handoff): run concurrency tests, finalize evaluation report and handoff docs.

Success criteria (proposed) — please confirm / modify:
- Accuracy: F1 >= 0.82 on our internal clinical summarization test set (you to provide labels or a labeled subset).
- Latency: 95th percentile tail latency <= 300 ms for typical request size (we can tighten if needed).
- Throughput: sustain 40 req/s with <= 10% error budget during a 30-minute spike test.
- Cost: estimated per-1M-token cost at or below the threshold we discussed (I put a placeholder in the attached spreadsheet).

Owners and commitment:
- Acme: Elena (POC lead) for dataset access and acceptance testing; ML Platform team to coordinate infra credentials.
- Redwood: Connor (SE) for deployment/config; Marissa (you can see I'm coordinating) for project management and success criteria signoff.

Next steps / asks:
- Elena: please confirm the success criteria above and share a representative test set (or a stub) by Fri 4/10.
- Acme infra: provide a list of allowed IPs and whether VPC or shared-hosted option preferred.
- Connor/Rishi: confirm availability for a 45-min kickoff next Tue or Wed (we suggested Tue 4/13 or Wed 4/14).

Attachments: Acme_POC_Playbook_v1.pdf (one-page timeline & checklist), redwood-eval-metrics-sheet.xlsx (metrics template).

If that plan looks good I'll lock in the kickoff and send a calendar invite.

Best,

Marissa Cole

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear plan and the materials. High-level: we like the scope and the 4-week cadence. A few notes from our side that will affect acceptance criteria and the kickoff prep:

1) Success criteria tweak: can we target 95th percentile latency <= 200 ms for common queries? Our production SLA is aggressive and we'd like to see if Redwood can meet tighter tails. If 200 ms is unrealistic at first pass, we can keep 300 ms as a stretch target.
2) Accuracy: the F1 target of 0.82 looks reasonable; we'll provide a labeled subset (~1k samples) for validation.
3) Data handling / infra: we will use a staging VPC and need KMS integration details. We also need to confirm whether any sample data must be de-identified before transfer (legal will advise).
4) Timeline: we can share the labeled subset by EOD Mon 4/12 if that works. Kickoff: Tue 4/13 at 11:00am PST is good for our team.

One ask: do you have a short checklist for our security team (SOC2 evidence, data residency notes) so I can accelerate internal approvals?

Elena Torres
Head of ML Platform
Acme Health
